notes: Sources opened: issue #89 body and comments (gh api) - marbosjo's report (quoted) with 'This bug does not happen in the tf2 cpp implementation neither in tf.'; tfoote's diagnosis (comment 83259331, quoted verbatim); mrath's 'Fixed with queue_size 100 in pull request #90.' and tfoote's closing 'Fixed in #90 '; transform_broadcaster.py at 1bbf9108 line 44 ('self.pub_tf = rospy.Publisher("/tf", TFMessage, queue_size=1)'), transform_listener.py line 52 ('rospy.Subscriber("/tf", TFMessage, self.callback)'), transform_broadcaster.cpp line 42 ('publisher_ = node_.advertise<tf2_msgs::TFMessage>("/tf", 100);') all via raw.githubusercontent; fix commit ede2646d (gh api): 'Merge pull request #90 from mrath/indigo-devel\n\nsame queue size of transform boradcaster in c++ and Python' (2015-03-20). Eligibility: agree, stop 6. E2 step 1: the broadcasting process (reporter's node hosting the tf2_ros Python TransformBroadcaster) and the subscribing process (tf2_tools view_frames hosting the tf2_ros TransformListener) interact only through the /tf topic and are separate units ('two nodes that interact only through ROS interfaces are separate units even when they ship in one package'; here in one repository, two packages). Step 2: the loss is a property of the interaction - the provider's outgoing queue depth versus the burst the consumer must receive; the C++ broadcaster (queue 100) with the same consumer does not lose messages, so the failure depends on the provider's queue property crossing the boundary, not on either unit alone. Steps 3-5: the fix changes the publisher's queue-depth value, not names, build, or firmware. Stop 6, topic. Failed condition: class DISAGREED - the recorded class qos_reliability is wrong: rospy Publisher queue_size is the outgoing message queue depth (history), and no reliability policy differs between the sides (ROS 1 transports are reliable); the spec's own notes state the class should be 'other' ('a history/queue-depth property with no dedicated class in the schema ... so it is recorded as other'), contradicting its own failed_conditions entry - proposed 'other'. Elements (topic:/tf) agreed. Loudness silent_documented/run agreed: the loss is visible only as missing frames in the view_frames graph, with no diagnostic from ROS tooling. Resolution recommended agreed: PR #90 merged as ede2646d and the issue closed, but neither the reporter nor the source shows the reproducer re-run against the merged revision, so the resolved composition is not shown working.
